newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen flat, limited impact from Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen flat, limited impact from Sakakibara.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures contract settled unchanged on Friday after recovering from early lows.

Comments on Japanese interest rates by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara this morning triggered light selling, but had a limited impact as he had made similar remarks earlier this month, traders said.
The December was at 99.07 after falling as low as 99.04.
Its session high was 99.09. Turnover was 60,809 contracts.

Sakakibara, director-general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, told Reuters it would be natural for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates when it has confirmed the strength of the economy.
He also said the possibility of the economy contracting was less than people thought and that it was dangerous to assume that Japan would not raise interest rates within a year.
Some traders said the remark had made them cautious about buying.

"Given that Sakakibara was making such comments for the second time this week, the topside was capped more heavily than before. The December's session high was 99.09 today from 99.11 on Thursday," a dealer at a city bank said.
It was the third time this month that Sakakibara has warned that Japan may end an era of record-low interest rates.

The dealer said other factors capping the topside included upward pressure in cash money market rates ahead of Japan's "Golden Week" holiday in late April and expectations that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto may try to boost Tokyo stocks before his meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton next week.
"Some people are afraid the Prime Minister may talk up Tokyo stocks next week to show Clinton that Japan's domestic demand is firm," the dealer said.
The key overnight call rate eased to 0.47 percent after the BOJ's more accommodative stance in the morning. But strong demand from banks for short-term funds underpinned the rate.
"It seems the BOJ had to check the rate's rise given several comments recently from people other than the BOJ on interest rates," said a trust bank dealer.
Key three-month certificates of deposit were issued at an unchanged 0.55 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
